Look at Fig. 15 and you'll see it right away: the alitrunk is swollen and rides much higher than the propodeal dorsum. The propodeum carries a pair of strong spines, straight to slightly upcurved. There's no metanotal groove. The metapleural lobes are triangular and conspicuous.

Now the petiole, in profile. It has an elongate peduncle and a well-developed node whose dorsum slopes down toward the rear, leaving a short posterior face. On the postpetiole, the anterior and dorsal surfaces run together into one convexity; the posterior face is truncated. From above, the nodes of both petiole and postpetiole are broader than long.

The head tells you more. Its dorsum is strongly longitudinally rugose, with 5–7 rugae between the frontal carinae at eye level. These rugae wander a little and are irregular, and a few anastomoses usually show up. The scrobal area is mostly smooth, though you'll usually find 1–2 fine rugulae crossing its width just behind the antennal fossa. Behind the eyes, the sides of the head are finely reticulate-rugose, and that sculpture wraps around the posterior margins of the scrobe to the occiput. Between the rugae? Nothing, or at most the faintest superficial traces.

The dorsal alitrunk is finely but strongly reticulate-rugose throughout, with broad, shining interspaces. The petiole dorsum is rugulose. The postpetiole varies, from rugulose to only faintly sculptured. The gaster is unsculptured. Covering all dorsal surfaces of head and body: dense, fine, acute hairs. Color runs from dark reddish brown to blackish brown.

UPO-06: PrhI Gene Synthesis
UPO-06 carries the coding sequence for prhI from *Ralstonia solanacearum*. PrhI is an ECF sigma factor, and transcription driven by the Prh signal transduction system depends on it. PrhR activates the gene first; the gene then directs sigma factor expression by switching on the PprhJ promoter. We optimized the sequence for expression in *Escherichia coli*.

UPO-11: PprhJ Promoter Synthesis
UPO-11 gives you the PprhJ promoter region. When the bacterium touches a plant cell, PrhA and PrhR pass the signal through, and the ECF sigma factor PrhI switches this promoter on. We optimized the sequence for expression in *Escherichia coli*.

Subject: Key Findings on foxl2 Expression Patterns in Trout

Dear Customer,

Here is what we found about foxl2 transcript expression in your study.

Both transcripts turn on very early in development (Figure 2). foxl2a stays highly restricted in the male. foxl2b, the diverged paralog, shows up in most adult extragonadal tissues we examined (see Additional file 2).

In adult females, foxl2b expression narrows to three tissues: skin, gill, and ovary. In the testis, it is very strong. That fits earlier work showing foxl2b present and foxl2a absent in later stages of testis development in trout [23].

Put together, these results point to foxl2b as a likely regulator of male-specific genes (such as cyp19b1), especially later in development.

[10] Consequently, they lack the essential attribute of additionality. Additionality examines the counterfactual: what would have happened under the status quo had the REC not been purchased or contracted. While many additionality testing frameworks exist, the core question stays the same: did the project's financial survival depend on REC revenues? Without verified proof of additionality, RECs cannot be treated as genuine emissions offsets.

We derived a time-dependent mild-slope equation, following the formal derivation of Smith & Sprinks (1975). From it, we obtained the higher-order dispersion relation for waves over an uneven bottom.

Then we used only the linear dispersion relation for steady waves and recovered equation (2.12) of Chamberlain & Porter (1995), the Modified Mild-Slope Equation (MMSE). At leading order, the modified curvature terms of the MMSE matter. The slope square terms do not, which fits the mild-slope assumption. So we kept every modified curvature term the MSE had dropped, and that gave us a uniform model.

To test it, we built a numerical model with the finite element method (FEM) that predicts wave scattering over a varying bottom. The uniform model captures the main features of waves over different sea beds, including sinusoidal beds and man-made bars. On sinusoidal beds, it matches the experimental data more closely than the other established models. On man-made bars, both the MMSE and the uniform model beat the results of Kirby (1986) against the same data.

One more thing worth your attention: the FEM model also handles wave transformation over arbitrarily-varying bathymetry.

Subject: A Note on the Enduring Legacy of Buraq

Dear Friend,

The world once existed as a blend of reality and myth, and the distinction between the two only emerged with modern comparative biology. Even so, science has not erased the liminal zone where a figure like Buraq resides. We need such transitional objects to connect seemingly divergent realms of empirical knowledge and spiritual experience.

Her presence in contemporary culture works as a bridge between rationalist taxonomies and the vestigial power of myth. This idea finds its most forceful expression in the Islamic transport industry, where Buraq, a figure combining piety and speed, recurs as a patron saint. She gives her name to airlines from Libya to Indonesia, bus companies, freight ships, motorcycle taxis, a space camp, an engineering college, and even Pakistan's first drone.

The fluidity of Buraq as an aesthetic and linguistic object explains her pliability in commercial use: she presides over wings and wheels, and is also used to sell plastic and PVC, heavy metal, and heavy-duty diesel (BURAQ LUBRICANTS), Indian food, and surgical instruments.

MapleStory Monsters: A Survival Guide to the Underworld

Welcome to MapleStory. There are thousands of monsters roaming the world, so here is a quick breakdown of where they live and how to survive.

The weak monsters are the most common foes, and they are found by towns. They wander aimlessly, even if you bump into them. Don't worry, just take the damage they deal.

The dangerous ones live deep in dungeons. Those are the most lethal monsters in the game.

Now for the aggro mechanic, which matters a lot. Monsters normally roam aimlessly, even if you bump into them. But if you attack an enemy or cast a debuff on it, you aggro it. That means you get its attention, and it will try to attack you back.

The behavioral pattern: most enemies attack by trying to run into you over and over again.

The best strategy against these persistent attackers is simple. Attack them repeatedly. Your attacks usually have enough knockback to keep them in place.

Sometimes you will need dodge tactics, meaning you jump over them to avoid their attacks entirely.

For the full details, check out the complete list at MapleStory/Monsters/Complete list.

Remember, aggro is a two-way street. Stay safe and keep attacking.

Later, geological uplift raised the Western Ghats Mountains. Children learn to speak in their first few years of life. If a child cannot hear, that window closes. Hearing impairment blocks speech, and it also blocks the ability to understand spoken language.

Often the first sign that a child is severely hearing-impaired (deaf) comes late, after communication problems have already strained the family and slowed social skills. A child raised in a Deaf community, where people sign instead of speak, avoids much of this (see our article on Deaf Culture).

That is why many developed countries test newborns for hearing. The goal is to stop a deaf child from being isolated inside a hearing family without anyone realizing it. Sign language is a complete means of communication, but literacy still depends on understanding speech. In most written language, the sound of a word is coded in symbols.

Someone who heard well enough to learn speech and reading keeps that ability even if hearing later fades. Someone who never heard well enough to learn to speak rarely reads well (see [4]). Most evidence points the same way: identify hearing impairment early, and a child with very insensitive hearing has a real chance of learning spoken language. Listening matters for a second language too.

The Revolution gave the French throne a new fate: it shattered it. Chasing equality, the people turned on their own comforts. The deep armchairs, the heavy draperies, the eider-down cushions, all the refinements we alone understood in the European family, got their owners imprisoned. Live in a spacious hotel set back from the street, within a court, away from its noise and smells, and you had your throat cut.

That settled elegant manners. They went out of fashion fast, and the barbarity of their successors still clings to us. Every day you see it: an elegant Grecian chair, the one that broke your arm, dumped in the lumber-room, beside canopies that stink of the stable because they are stuffed with hay.

Transduction is how your body turns physical and chemical signals into neural impulses. In the nervous system, it's the basic process of converting stimuli into electrical signals. Sensory receptors do this work: they take physical or chemical inputs and turn them into electrical impulses that travel to your brain.

Look at your visual system. In the retina, rod and cone cells connect the physical world to neural communication. Light strikes these photoreceptors and changes the shape of the protein rhodopsin. That shift sets off a cascade of events that alters the photoreceptor's electrochemical gradient. As the gradient drops, so do the electrical signals sent to your brain. Which means more light hitting the photoreceptor produces fewer electrical impulses. Your brain reads that inverse pattern and decodes the visual world with precision.

Subject: Hitchhiking in the Ruhr Area: Read This First

Dear Customer,

The Ruhr Area (German: Ruhrgebiet), or just the Ruhr, is an urban region in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It's a chain of former industrial cities: Duisburg, Oberhausen, Bottrop, Mülheim an der Ruhr, Essen, Gelsenkirchen, Bochum, Herne, Hamm, Hagen, Dortmund, Recklinghausen, Unna, Witten.

Five million people live here. That's far more than Berlin, Hamburg, or Munich. The motorway network is dense, yet hitchhiking here is hard. The problem is the web of minor roads. The main motorways are the A1, A2, and A3.

So if you're hitching through, stick to those three. Stay off the smaller roads; almost no transit traffic uses them. Germany treats hitchhikers well almost everywhere, but the Ruhr is the country's worst spot for it. Think of it like hitching in Istanbul. The cities are independent, but to a traveler they blur into one massive city.

Plan well, and travel safely.

Best regards,

Subject: Study Results: Lung Tissue Volume and Aeration Analysis

Dear Customer,

Here are the key findings from our analysis of lung tissue volume and functional changes.

We calculated total lung tissue volume as: number of voxels × volume of the voxel, for any compartment with a CT number above zero.

The change in functional residual capacity from PEEP withdrawal (ΔFRC) is the difference in total gas volume in the whole lung between PEEP and ZEEP states. Alveolar derecruitment is the difference in gas volume within poorly aerated and nonaerated lung regions between these same conditions.

We also measured the gas volume lost to PEEP withdrawal in normally aerated regions, defined by CT attenuations between -500 and -900 HU (see Figure 2).

Following reference [21], we classified each patient's lost lung aeration (lung morphology) as diffuse, patchy, or lobar, based on the distribution of CT attenuations at ZEEP.

Mobile Gaming: The Next Evolution of Co-Creation

If you tell stories for a living, pay attention to what mobile internet is doing to games. Portable, location-aware interfaces are pulling electronic games into a new phase of a decades-long evolution, one where the player stops being just an avatar in someone else's gameworld and starts co-authoring it with the original designers.

Here's what makes that possible. Location-aware interfaces let players fold real places into the gameworld, and the gameworld back into real places. No interactive media had done that before. And mobile games don't stop at worldmaking. They abandon linear narratives in favor of cooperative storytelling that runs on your experience of place.

The "author-player" idea itself isn't new. What's new is how mobile games push it past the limits of the traditional video game. The worldmaking leaves the screen and enters physical space, and location-aware interfaces turn what you see, hear, and feel in real places into storytelling tools.

In our essay, we theorize the unique storytelling potential of mobile games and then describe what happened when we tried to use it ourselves, designing and implementing our hybrid-reality game, University of Death.
